limitations: No main merge, production deployment/migration/write, real provider, signer, key, chain call, actual account signup, messages to people or live funds.

The new coordinator uses actual stored credential and canonical SQL contracts, but every database/account/session/asset in verification is synthetic; no real login, product route or native application screen is exercised.
The new initial namespace and one-request activation are separate from the older amount-correction namespace. Existing v1/v2/v3 financial contracts, schemas and fixture bytes remain unchanged.

The first initial wallet cohort refuses competing target-listing reservations, progressed requests and unpaired active seller wallet trades. The general seller three-trade policy is unchanged; two other canonical commitments may precede the proposed third.

Activation records a verified mapping and clean pending basis, not seller consent. Acceptance requires a fresh stored seller principal with canSell and exact request seller identity on both new actions and retries.

Unknown-COMMIT evidence injects a lost reply after a real PostgreSQL COMMIT. It is not a physical network-partition test; recovery inspects the same target and returns the original receipt without replacement work.

There is no supported combined backup/restore format for the new initial namespace. Existing isolated v3 and amount-correction formats fail closed. Reopening the same durable database is not portable disaster recovery.
All three new native fixture databases finish paused; there is no v3 resume or later payment/cancellation/dispute/release/settlement command.
Canonical notification rows and a safe immutable publication intent are committed, but no external delivery service or sender is installed or invoked.
The earlier isolated v3 native drill retains its financial-only synthetic scope, and the earlier initial canonical mechanics drill remains its separate pause-only companion fixture.
Session revocation is ordered by actual shared locks; authorization/expiry is checked at explicit checkpoints, not against the wall-clock arrival of the COMMIT acknowledgement.

The development runtime fence conservatively serializes canonical dependency writes. It is not a production throughput or high-availability design; database-superuser resistance and production roles are not established by GUC/context checks.
The Chromium gate is the retained standalone English/Arabic rehearsal, not a new initial-acceptance product screen or actual platform authentication flow.
Root TypeScript excludes apps/mobile and three existing test paths. No native application build, full production build, independent security audit or live readiness is claimed.

Combined initial-cohort recovery, later trade lifecycle, broader identity-bound cohorts, real web/mobile product integration, custody/provider/signing decisions and operational launch gates remain open.
